result.text:
All 40 tests pass. Here's what I changed, item by item.

**1–2. Instantiation.** `Floor.with_rooms_and_prices(n, prices)` and `Hotel.with_floors(floors)` are class-side creation messages that validate first and then call `__init__`, which leaves the object fully initialized — no more `None` instance variables and no `set_number_of_rooms` / `set_prices` / `set_floors`. The tests' `create_floor_with_and` and `create_hotel` now use them.

**3. Room states.** `Room` holds a `RoomState`: `AvailableRoomState`, `ReservedRoomState`, `OccupiedRoomState` (which is the only one that knows a guest type), all in `room.py`. The `"reserved"` magic guest type, the `None` guest and the unused `Room.guest_type` accessor are gone.

**4. No repetition in the transitions.** `RoomState` implements `receive` / `receive_with_reservation` / `reserve` as the error each state gives by default; every subclass redefines only the transition it accepts and returns the new state. `Room`'s three methods are one delegation each: `self._state = self._state.receive(...)`.

**5. Encapsulation.** `Floor.rooms()` is deleted. `Floor` answers `receive_at_room`, `receive_with_reservation_at_room`, `reserve_room`, and validates room numbers itself in a private `room_at`. Since room numbers are now the floor's knowledge, the description lives in `Floor.room_number_does_not_exist_error_description()`; `Hotel`'s static delegates to it so the existing assertions keep working.

**6. Losses.** Added `Room.loss_using_if_absent_guest_type` — max price for an available room, 0 otherwise (the base state returns 0, only `AvailableRoomState` redefines it). Tests 13–15 no longer use `should_fail`, and `should_fail`, now unused, was removed. `Floor.total_losses` asks every room for its loss, mirroring `total_profits`.

**7. Repeated code.** The index loops are gone: `Hotel.total_of(...)` and `Floor.total_of(...)` sum over floors/rooms and are reused by profits, losses and every total; `Floor.total_rooms_satisfying(...)` backs the three counters; the three `Hotel` guest methods are one delegation each through the private `floor_at`. `Hotel.total_rooms_available` is now derived from its floors instead of the hand-maintained `_available_rooms_count` (which was decremented on `receive`/`reserve` but never elsewhere).

**8. Bonus.** Floor tests use the new floor protocol instead of reaching into rooms (the `# Tech Debt` comments are gone); guest types, prices and creation methods moved to `SimsHotelsTestSupport` in `tests/sims_hotels_test_support.py`, inherited by the three test cases; `HotelTest` got `create_hotel_with(*floors)` and an `assert_is_empty(hotel)` used by tests 9–12. I also added one test (`FloorTest.test10`) covering the room-number check now owned by `Floor` — that's the 40th test.

Two judgment calls worth flagging: `loss_using_if_absent_guest_type` never evaluates the if-absent block (an occupied room loses nothing, so its guest type is not consulted) — the parameter exists only to mirror `profit_using_if_absent_guest_type`, as the given tests require. And I appended a section to `README.md` describing the post-refactor state, since the rest of that file documents the starting code.
